text:
jamal: Spinning up the new eu-berlin GPU pool. Quick validation run planned now — kernel/driver checks, throughput baseline, and a short handoff doc. Ping me if you want in the call.
sara: on it. I'll run the nvdriver check and a small gRPC echo benchmark first.
kevin: I'll watch node health and networking. Watch out for MTU differences on the berlin fabric (we hit 1500 vs 9000 previously).
jamal: plan: 1) driver + cuda sanity 2) small transformer throughput (batch 1/4/16) 3) p95 latency baseline with our proxy 4) collect dmesg / nvidia-smi logs 5) handoff checklist.
sara: running `sudo modinfo nvidia` now. Driver: 535.86.05, CUDA toolkit visible at /usr/local/cuda-12.1.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] new node pool eu-berlin-rtx: 6 nodes added, instance type rtx-a5000-24gb, kernel 6.1.53.
kevin: kernel 6.1.53 is ok but we need `nvidia-uvm` loaded — if not, restart `nvidia-persistenced`.
sara: `lsmod | grep nvidia` shows nvidia_uvm 131072 0; nvidia 2863104 2. good. running quick `./bench/grpc_echo --concurrency 8`
sara: results: batch=1 throughput=420 req/s, p50=2.1ms, p95=8.9ms. batch=4 throughput=1630 req/s, p95=22ms. batch=16 failed with OOM on one node (logs attached).
jamal: OOM likely due to default pod_resource_request too small for that batch. For now set per-pod mem request to 60Gi for batch>=16 tests. Also check our cudaMalloc limits.
kevin: checked dmesg: one node shows "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" around test time — driver recovered but that's likely a power/thermals issue. Fan curve look ok, but BIOS power limit was at 210W. Raising to 250W for the next run.
sara: re-run after power limit bump: batch=16 throughput=5400 req/s, p95=85ms, tail spikes at ~300ms during gc. Logs: `OOM` -> resolved.
infra-bot: [monitor] node eu-berlin-rtx-3 reported GPU temp 92C during run.
kevin: temp 92C is high; we should set longer warmup and avoid 30min sustained full-power runs until ops confirms airflow. Marking node-3 as degraded for now.
jamal: noted. For the baseline report we exclude node-3 and rerun single-run metrics across remaining 5 nodes. Also start driver regression check against canary branch (we pinned driver 535).
sara: rerun p95 baseline excluding node-3: batch=1 p95=8.5ms, batch=4 p95=20ms, batch=16 p95=78ms stable. Profiling shows kernel launch latencies stable, KV cache hitrate ~71%.
kevin: network check: iperf3 between controller and nodes shows ~9.2Gbps avg (expected 10Gbps), few retransmits around 00:03. MTU at 9000 on infra routers but some fabric switches set 1500 on UPS links -> causing occasional fragmentation. Filed ticket #INF-492 to unify MTU.
jamal: cost note: current instance type avg on-demand cost ~2.6x compared to us-west baseline. Need to calculate qps/cost for dedicated capacity offering before handoff. I'll run cost per 1k requests metric.
sara: added a small smoke test script to repo: ```bash
# quick smoke
./run_bench --model small-llama --batch 4 --duration 120 --collect-metrics > berlin-smoke.log
```
kevin: I've prepared the handoff checklist stub: - nodes healthy (no GPU falloff) - driver + cuda verified - MTU ticket open - thermal remediation plan - p95 baselines documented - cost qps/cost calc attached - canary traffic plan
jamal: filling the baseline doc now and will attach artifacts (nvidia-smi dumps, dmesg, bench logs). After I attach, can we get product on a quick review for rollout gating?
sara: log uploads done to S3: s3://redwood-infra/bench/eu-berlin/1767809211/ (contains bench logs and profile traces).
infra-bot: [audit] artifacts uploaded by sara at 2026-03-18T14:17:10Z
kevin: ok I'm scheduling a nodes-only maintenance window to cycle node-3 fans and check airflow Monday 08:00 UTC.
jamal: handoff: assigning to oncall@redwood for canary next week. Action items: jamal->finalize baseline doc, kevin->MTU ticket + thermal, sara->update smoke script with retries and mem requests. If all green we'll flip canary at 10% traffic next Tue. :thumbsup:
kevin: :+1: I'll add a note in the runbook about increasing `nvidia_pci_replay_count` if we see GPU off bus again.
sara: leaving one last note: driver 535 had a known GPU reset bug on older BIOS; we should pin BIOS rev >= 1.2.0 for newer machines.
jamal: thanks team. I'll post the final baseline doc here when complete and close the thread.
